newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG EXTENDS WORLD CUP LEAD WITH WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG EXTENDS WORLD CUP LEAD WITH WIN.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg intimidated her rivals by breezing down an icy German hill to clinch her third slalom victory of the Alpine skiing season on Sunday and extend her lead in the overall World Cup.
While several big names lost control on a difficult piste, the double world champion skied with flair but composure to seal her fifth World Cup triumph of the season with two almost faultless runs.

After her third and fourth places in giant slaloms in the German resort on Friday and Saturday, the slalom triumph gave the softly-spoken Swede a 328-point over Germany's defending champion Katja Seizinger in the overall World Cup.

Wiberg is now close to clinching the slalom World Cup title. With just three races remaining, she already has a 215-point lead over second-placed Italian Deborah Compagnoni, who finished third on Sunday behind Austrian Elfi Eder.
Seizinger, who failed to get any points in one of the giant slaloms after an embarrassing fall, took seventh place in the slalom, a good result for the German in the discipline.

"That was one of the fastest slaloms on the tour. It was easy to ski out of it," Wiberg said. "I really wanted to win this one. It's great to win like this and get closer to my main goal of the season -- the slalom World Cup."
"It has been a great weekend. But I still don't want to talk about the overall World Cup."
Wiberg clocked an aggregate time of one minute 33.52 seconds, a comfortable 1.69 seconds ahead of Eder who took second with 1:35.21.
Compagnoni, who won both of the Zwiesel giant slaloms, completed a successful three days of racing in Germany with her third place in 1:35.60.
Wiberg had a 0.82-second lead over Eder after the first run. None of the her rivals looked capable of challenging her and some racers found the conditions impossible.
In the first run Slovenia's world bronze medallist Urska Hrovat fell after crossing her skis. Experienced Austrian Anita Wachter and Swiss Karin Roten missed gates.
The snow was slightly softer for the second run when New Zealand's Claudia Riegler, third fastest in the first run, lost control of her inner ski at a gate and crashed out.

Compagnoni's excellent form in Germany has left her third in the overall rankings, 90 points behind Seizinger. She will now bid to win her first World Cup race on home territory next weekend in Cortina d'Ampezzo.
